key_insight: Classical simulation dominates the practical cost of near-term QNLP: the VQC is often much slower than a matched classical baseline, and only a small fraction of configurations show any clear accuracy gain.
engineering_relevance: For quantum ML practitioners, simulator runtime is the main feasibility bottleneck to budget, profile, and optimize before expecting algorithmic advantages.
method: PennyLane state-vector VQC on SST-2 sentiment classification
27-grid sweep over qubits (4/6/8), training sizes (200/500/1000), and depths
Compared against PCA-matched logistic regression and uncompressed TF-IDF logistic regression
evidence_signal: Across 27 single-seed runs, the VQC won only 6 times; after additional seeds, only 1 case retained a positive mean advantage, while training was 886–21,127× slower than the matched classical fit.
watch_item: Results come from one dataset, one ansatz, one simulator, and one CPU setup, so they show feasibility cost rather than a general performance verdict.
paper_title: What Does It Cost to Simulate a Quantum Sentence Classifier? An Energy and Compute Perspective on Near-Term QNLP
